chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! This (illness) which has appeared on my face, the people allege that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not afflict any servant with it for whom He has a need.'

So he said to me: 'No! It was so that a believer of the people of Pharaoh was paralysed in his fingers, so he was saying like this' – and he extended his hand, and he was saying: 'O people! Follow the Messengers.'

He said, 'Then he said: When it is the last third of the night, during its beginning, perform ablution and stand to your prayer which you tend to pray. So when you are in the last prostration of the first two cycles, so say:'

While you are prostrating: 'O Ali! O Exalted! O Magnificent! O Beneficent! O Merciful! O Hearer of the supplications and O Giver of the goodness! Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and Give me from the goodness of the world and the Hereafter, what You are Rightful of it, and Exchange from me from the evil of the world and the Hereafter what You are Rightful of it, and Remove from me this pain' – and specify it – 'for it has infuriated me and grieved me', and be insistent in the supplication'.
He said, 'So I had not even arrived at Al-Kufa until Allah removed it from me, all of it.'

key_terms.الثُّلُثُ الْأَخِيرُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ: The last third of the night

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication for removing facial illness according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual efficacy of supplication during the last third of the night, linking physical healing to the example of the 'Believer of Pharaoh's Family' who, despite his paralysis, remained a steadfast advocate for Moses. The narrative underscores the Shia tradition of viewing specific ailments as opportunities for divine connection, where reciting the prescribed du'a leads to the complete removal of the affliction upon reaching Kufa.
